sixC.title: We weave the 6Cs into every project
sixC.lede: The 6Cs are our lens on the process; the spotlight stays on computational thinking—thinking, creating, and coding with purpose.

c1.label: Communication
c1.body: Explain ideas, decisions and learnings: what was done, why, and what was learned when solving a challenge.

c2.label: Collaboration
c2.body: Work with others in an organized way: roles, coordination, listening, and building together.

c3.label: Artifact creation
c3.body: Produce tangible outputs that show learning: algorithms, paths, prototypes or clear explanations.

c4.label: Creativity
c4.body: Try multiple solutions, compare strategies and justify choices, embracing error as part of the process.

c5.label: Personal conduct
c5.body: Handle mistakes, give and receive feedback, respect others’ ideas, and act responsibly in technical work.

c6.label: Community
c6.body: Build a culture of shared learning: show your work, value others’, and learn collectively.

sixC.footer: With the 6Cs, computational thinking shapes autonomous, reflective, collaborative learners aware of how they learn and coexist.

block1.title: We teach coding from age 5
block1.body: Computational thinking scales with the learner: a shared logic from visual tools up to professional languages.
block1.item1: Breaks complex problems into clear steps.
block1.item2: Uses patterns and abstraction to reuse solutions.
block1.item3: With young kids we use visual languages that require no reading or writing; as they grow they move to JavaScript, Python, C++, and Go.

block2.title: Screen-free to start
block2.body: We use educational robotics and a screen-light curriculum: Thymio with LEDs, sounds, sensors keeps focus on logic before code.
block2.step1: Think: define inputs/outputs the robot shows (LEDs, sound, movement).
block2.step2: Plan: sequence with cards and pseudocode, then send to the robot.
block2.step3: Code & test: move to code, debug, and see the physical response.

block3.title: Culturally respectful activities
block3.body: We design challenges with local languages, stories, and trades so technology keeps identity alive and builds community pride.
block3.item1: Co-create with teachers and local leaders to adapt examples and symbols.
block3.item2: Use materials and scenarios from the territory before moving to robots or screens.
block3.item3: Document in plain language so families can join.

about.title: Who we are?
about.subtitle: A foundation that articulates governments, academia, and companies so that innovation becomes an engine of peace
about.description: We are a non-profit organization dedicated to bringing education in science, technology, and innovation to vulnerable communities. We work with a territorial approach that respects and enhances Colombia's cultural diversity.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: Democratize access to STEAM education through contextualized programs that strengthen local capacities and generate sustainable development opportunities in vulnerable territories.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.text: To be recognized as leaders in transformative education that connects innovation, territory, and peace, positively impacting more than 100,000 people by 2030.
